sources.note: The base layer. Every surface, ramp stop and interaction state starts here.

sources.label: @okouai/platform
sources.note: Loaded on top of the base layer by the product. What it redeclares, it wins.

sections.title: Brand scale
sections.blurb: Amber, adopted stop-for-stop from the published palette. The brand stop is 300, not the 700 the pre-rebrand orange used, and it is the same fill in both themes.

tokens.name: --primary-0
tokens.comment:
Primary Color Scale (Amber). Adopted stop-for-stop from the palette, so
the brand colour is 300 and the scale darkens monotonically from there.
Only `--primary-0` is generated, above the published 50.

sections.title: Neutral ramp
sections.blurb: Anchored on Linen (#FAF5F3) and Ink (#242321). Contrast, not equal numeric spacing, sets the text end: 600 clears 3:1, 700 clears 4.5:1.

tokens.name: --gray-0
tokens.comment:
Neutral Gray Color Scale (Light). Linen is exact at 100, Ink at 950;
intermediate chroma tapers toward zero in OKLab.

sections.title: Surfaces & text
sections.blurb: The semantic layer components actually reference. Everything here resolves into the two ramps above.

tokens.name: --background
tokens.comment:
The page sits one step above the ramp, because `gray-50` is the app's
neutral *fill* (chips, icon containers, inset panels, mobile bars). If
the page took gray-50 as well, every one of those fills would vanish
against it. Linen sits one step below at gray-100, carrying the heavier
chrome -- sidebar, muted, accent, secondary.

The canvas is white and untinted. It is over half of a chat frame, and
everything else is read against it, so warmth there reads as dirt
rather than as character. Cards are white too and sit flush with it,
read from their border and shadow the way the design reference does.
`gray-50` and `gray-200` sit on the canvas and keep only a trace of
warmth; `gray-0` and Linen are chrome and keep theirs.
#FFFFFF - the canvas carries no tint

tokens.name: --background-50
tokens.comment: gray-50 - lighter background for code blocks

tokens.name: --foreground
tokens.comment:
Body copy drops the ramp's hue. Every other stop keeps 42.9, but at
paragraph scale a warm near-black reads as a cast rather than as
black. The two nav columns stay on Ink through `--sidebar-foreground`,
so chrome keeps the hue and only content loses it.
#242424 - hue-less near-black

tokens.name: --input
tokens.comment: gray-200 - lighter than card for visible input surfaces

tokens.name: --input-border-radius
tokens.comment:
Input System
Design tokens for consistent input styles across the application
Applied automatically to all input and textarea elements
rounded-lg

tokens.name: --muted
tokens.comment: gray-200 - lighter than card for visible inner surfaces

tokens.name: --on-filled
tokens.comment:
Text on filled/colored backgrounds (buttons, tooltips, badges)
Pure white for text on colored backgrounds

tokens.name: --overlay
tokens.comment:
Dialog scrim. Deliberately NOT theme-aware: --black inverts to #FFFFFF
in dark, which would lighten the backdrop instead of dimming it. The
dark theme reuses this value and only raises the alpha.
#242321 - Ink

tokens.name: --primary-foreground
tokens.comment:
Amber is a light fill and cannot carry white text (1.97:1). Ink clears
7.95:1 and is the same in both themes, because the fill is too.
#242321 - Ink

tokens.name: --sidebar
tokens.comment:
Half the depth of the site's #FAF5F3 theme grey. This surface no longer
only backs the chat column: it also frames the workspace card, so it
reads as a border around white rather than as a panel beside it, and at
full strength that frame overpowered the sheet it holds. Lightness moves
to the midpoint with white while saturation holds, which halves the
channel spread by the same factor and keeps the hue intact.
gray-50 - chat column, one step off the canvas

sections.title: Status & brand text
sections.blurb: Coral carries both destructive and interrupt. Interrupting a run is not destruction, so it sits two stops lighter on the same ramp.

tokens.name: --brand-subtle
tokens.comment: Brand as a wash and as text (published brand-subtle / brand-text).

tokens.name: --interrupt
tokens.comment:
Interrupting a run is not destruction -- nothing is lost and the work is
resumable -- so it steps two stops up the same Coral ramp: still clearly
an interruption, but without the delete button's weight. Coral 500
carries white at 3.01:1, over the 3:1 an icon has to clear, and the
white square is the stop glyph everyone already reads.
#FF6030 - Coral 500

sections.title: Interaction states
sections.blurb: One ladder for every hover, selected and pressed background. Translucent layers for elements with no fill of their own; pre-mixed pairs for elements that already carry one.

tokens.name: --state-layer
tokens.comment:
Interaction state ladder (light).

The layer colour is chosen so that compositing it onto a surface lands
back on the neutral ramp rather than just darkening it. It is solved
from the step it has to produce: at `--state-hover-alpha` over a white
card this colour composites to gray-100's lightness, while higher alphas
keep the states ordered without introducing another hue.

sections.title: Segment control
sections.blurb: The selected segment needs its own pair: in dark, --card sits below the track, so a card-filled segment reads recessed instead of selected.

tokens.name: --segment-selected
tokens.comment:
Segment control (light): white lifts off the track.
The track takes gray-200 rather than the `--muted` gray-100 the base
theme uses. Against a white canvas gray-100 clears 1.06:1, so both the
track and the white selection dissolve into the page and the control
stops reading as a control. Dark already tracks on gray-200.

sections.title: Data colours
sections.blurb: Credit and usage breakdowns. These are literal hexes on purpose — a chart series must stay separable, which the neutral ramp cannot guarantee.

tokens.name: --color-credit-free
tokens.comment: Credit balance breakdown segment colors (usage bar chart)

tokens.name: --color-usage-kind-model
tokens.comment:
Usage record kind breakdown segment colors. Model uses a cool indigo so
the dominant LLM segment separates cleanly from the pink image hue; image
and video also sit far apart (pink vs teal).

sections.title: Typography
sections.blurb: Geist and Geist Mono, set by the platform layer. The base layer still names Noto Sans; the platform override is what the product renders.

tokens.name: --font-family-emoji
tokens.light: "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Color Emoji", sans-serif
tokens.dark: "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Color Emoji", sans-serif
tokens.comment:
Color-emoji fonts must come first so dual-presentation codepoints (e.g. the
"squared CJK" buttons 🈶🈯🈹) resolve to their color glyph instead of the
text glyph a CJK text font would otherwise supply.

sections.title: Icon system
sections.blurb: Lucide emits a 2px stroke when nothing overrides it. The base layer normalises that to 1.5 for every icon that has not opted out.

tokens.name: --color-brand-subtle
tokens.comment:
Brand Tint / Brand Text

The Amber scale is no longer mirrored between themes, so a raw stop like
`primary-100` is a pale tint in light and still a pale tint in dark, where
it would blow out. These two are theme-aware: reach for them wherever the
brand appears as a wash behind text or as text itself, and keep the raw
stops for fills that already pair with `--primary-foreground`.

tokens.name: --color-segment-selected
tokens.comment:
Segment Control

The track reuses `--muted`, which already steps down the ramp in both
themes (gray-100 light, gray-200 dark). The selected segment has to read
as raised above that track, and `--card` cannot carry it: in dark, card
sits *below* gray-200, so a card-filled segment would look recessed
instead of selected. It gets its own pair of tokens instead.

tokens.name: --color-sidebar-border
tokens.comment: Sidebar colors - using tokens for dark mode support

tokens.name: --color-state-hover
tokens.comment:
Interaction States

One ladder for every hover / selected / pressed background in the product.

`state-*` are translucent layers, so the same token reads with the same
weight on any surface (page, card, popover, nav) and reverses automatically
in dark mode. Use them on elements that have no opaque background of their
own -- rows, menu items, icon buttons, ghost buttons.

Elements that do carry an opaque fill cannot use a translucent layer
(the layer would replace the fill instead of sitting on it), so each fill
gets its own pre-mixed pair below.
